architectureDecisions: D1 — resolve() delegates candidate collection to the delivered retrievalPlanner.execute(requirement,{remainingBudget}) and no longer iterates planned.work itself. execute() already applies per-work item/byte reservations, groups by evidence and returns {planned, candidates, unresolved, failures}.

D2 — consumed.providerCalls = execute().planned.reserved.providerCalls. Reservation-based accounting is the budget-relevant quantity (each reservation counts against maxProviderCalls, and it bounds executed calls from above); the delivered execute() output does not expose an exact executed-call count and changing the planner is out of scope. The value is never floored with Math.max(...,1).
D3 — Items are built from execute().candidates in planner order with rank per evidence; the hard-coded slice(0,3) is removed because the planner already reserved at most budget.maxItems work units.

D4 — Materialization bytes via the delivered contract only: pass 1 calls defineContextResolution with consumed.materializedBytes = requirement.budget.maxMaterializedBytes; its returned materialization.bytes is the exact contract-computed size. Pass 2 rebuilds with consumed.materializedBytes = that exact value. resolutionId excludes consumed, so both passes share identity. A pass-1 rejection "consumed below materialization" means overflow and triggers D5. No serialization is re-implemented in the facade.

D5 — Budget overflow: if the exact materialization bytes exceed budget.maxMaterializedBytes, the facade drops the lowest-priority OPTIONAL evidence items first, then marks remaining overflowing evidence BUDGET_EXHAUSTED; status is recomputed (REQUIRED unresolved => UNSATISFIED). It never constructs a resolution that violates the budget and never throws for budget.

D6 — Unresolved reasons: planner unresolved and execute() unresolved/failure reasons (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, SOURCE_FAILURE, STALE, CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIABLE, UNSUPPORTED, AMBIGUOUS, MISSING) are copied verbatim; MISSING is used only when no candidate and no typed reason exists.

D7 — Thrown errors remain only for (a) invalid requirement/contract input, (b) STALE_DURING_RESOLUTION currentness drift (DurabilityFailure, unchanged), (c) catalog/planner misconfiguration. ProviderFailure no longer escapes resolve().
D8 — Durability reuse path and metadata passthrough are unchanged; the durability error discrimination keeps its current behavior (out of scope).

D9 — Regression tests live in test/oracle-facade-accounting.test.mjs and reproduce each probe case from docs/blackboard/evidence/BB-087/facade-probe.mjs with corrected expectations; the probe script itself is research evidence and is not modified.
implementationSlices: B1 — Regression first [FA1, FA2, FA3]: write test/oracle-facade-accounting.test.mjs reproducing the four probe cases (small budget, constant bytes, provider failure, dropped planner reason) plus over-budget and zero-provider-call cases; confirm they fail against the current facade.

B2 — Planner execution [FA2, INV-3, INV-4]: replace the manual planned.work loop with retrievalPlanner.execute() per D1-D3 and D6-D7; typed failures become unresolved entries and status is derived from necessity.

B3 — Truthful accounting + budget [FA1, INV-1, INV-2]: compute exact materialization bytes (two-pass contract) and reserved provider calls per D2, D4 and apply the D5 overflow rule so no resolution violates its budget.

An OPTIONAL evidence whose provider fails must return PARTIAL with its typed reason while REQUIRED evidence stays resolved.

A requirement whose evidence is all UNSUPPORTED (zero reservations) must report providerCalls 0, never a floored 1.
